items.summary: Approve containment-only execution. Do not create new implementation requests, requeue unchanged failures, deploy, add dependencies, collect telemetry, spend, expand monetization, or conduct external outreach. Continue only existing measurement, repair-or-close, attribution reconciliation, launch-readiness, and security evidence work. Preserve unavailable attribution, cost, margin, ROI, causal-lift, and readiness fields as unknown.

The three CRO concepts are technically plausible only as deferred, isolated prototypes. They are not adoption approvals, queue entries, production changes, or telemetry requests. Any future prototype requires disposable isolation, explicit input rights, dependency and security review, deterministic validation, measurable acceptance criteria, and deletion or rollback evidence.

Maintain parked/private factory candidates and existing measurement windows. No new site implementation is technically cleared while delivery is full, measurement backlog and failed requests remain open, and ownership, operations, or security evidence is incomplete.
